mainTopic: רבי יהודה's גזירות (financial panic and confusion), and the deadlines for eating חמץ on ערב פסח compared with how much witnesses err about the time.
overview: This amud begins by finishing the גמרא's explanation of why רבי יהודה forbids even 'safe' bloodletting on a sick בכור. His reason is that a person panics over his property (אדם בהול על ממונו) and may go on to make a מום. The חכמים use the same fact to argue for leniency instead. The גמרא then challenges this from a משנה about combing an animal on יום טוב, where רבי יהודה permits the gentle comb (קרצוף). The answer is that a dying animal causes panic, but an animal that is only uncomfortable does not. A second question asks why רבי יהודה makes a גזירה about חמץ but not about combing. The answer is that bread is easily confused with bread, while two different combs are not. Next comes a new משנה about the deadline for eating and burning חמץ on ערב פסח, with three opinions: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה (including the signal of the two תודה loaves), and רבן גמליאל. The גמרא connects this dispute to a משנה about witnesses who disagree on the hour. אביי then explains, in two versions, how much error in telling time each תנא assumes, and the second version continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה forbids bloodletting a sick בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי יהודה's reason. Because a person panics over his property, permitting a safe spot may lead him to cut a spot that makes a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A person panics] about his property, so we say: if you allow him to let blood in a spot that does not make a blemish, he will come to do it in a spot that does make a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing its explanation of why רבי יהודה won't allow even 'safe' bloodletting on a sick בכור. He fears that the panicked owner will go further and make a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner (the כהן) is desperate to save the animal, because a dead בכור can't be eaten. רבי יהודה reasons that a desperate person doesn't stop at the permitted line. So he forbids even the permitted kind of bloodletting as a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person panics/is agitated over his property
A blemish (making one in a בכור is forbidden)
He will come to do [the forbidden act]

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'עַל מָמוֹנוֹ' complete the phrase 'אדם בהול על ממונו' earlier.

phrases.english: about his property; [therefore] we say:
phrases.notes: This finishes the thought from the line before: a person panics about his property.

phrases.english: if you permit him
[to let blood] in a spot that does not make a blemish in it
he will come to do it
in a spot that does make a blemish in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָמוֹנוֹ, אָמְרִינַן: אִי שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer begun earlier: the בכור case differs because of financial panic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing reason: financial panic justifies a גזירה here specifically.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's ruling on the בכור might seem like a general tendency to make גזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is driven by the special concern that an owner panics over losing his animal.

steps.title: The חכמים turn the same logic around
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that because the owner panics, we must give him a permitted option. Otherwise he will surely do the forbidden act.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן [say]: all the more so [should we permit], for if you don't permit him anything at all, he will come to do [the forbidden act].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חכמים' side. They accept that the owner panics, but they reach the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the owner is desperate. רבי יהודה says to block everything so he won't go too far. The חכמים say a desperate person with no legal outlet will break the rule anyway, so giving him a permitted option protects against sin.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same fact (the owner panics over his property). רבי יהודה uses it to be strict, and the חכמים use it to be lenient.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis [say]:
all the more so [should it be permitted],
for if you do not permit him anything at all,
he will come to do [the forbidden act].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view's reasoning, completing the explanation of the dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that financial panic always argues for strictness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים hold that panic argues for giving a permitted outlet.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יהודה permits gentle combing on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really worries about financial panic. In a משנה, he allows the gentle comb on יום טוב without fearing that the owner will move on to the harsh one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we really say that according to רבי יהודה a person panics over his property? But we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says one may not scrape an animal on יום טוב, because he makes a wound, but one may scratch it. And the חכמים say one may not scrape, and also may not scratch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave for רבי יהודה. It cites a משנה where he does NOT make a protective גזירה even though an owner cares about his animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combing an itchy animal is also something an owner cares about. If רבי יהודה feared a panicked owner would go too far, he should forbid the gentle comb too, as the חכמים do. Since he permits it, it seems he does not apply the 'panic' concern.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really say...? (opens a challenge)
A wound, which is forbidden to make on יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. Here רבי יהודה is the lenient one and the חכמים are strict, which is the opposite of the בכור case. That reversal is exactly what creates the challenge.

phrases.english: And do we say, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
that a person panics over his property?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One may not scrape an animal on a Festival,
because he makes a wound,
but one may scratch [it].
And the Sages say:
One may not scrape, and also may not scratch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָדָם בָּהוּל עַל מָמוֹנוֹ? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in steps 1–2 for רבי יהודה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds a person panics over his property and therefore makes a גזירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the combing case, the owner also cares about his animal, yet רבי יהודה permits the gentle comb without fearing escalation. This contradicts attributing the 'panic' concern to him.

steps.title: Defining the two kinds of combing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the terms. קידור uses small teeth and makes a wound, while קרצוף uses large teeth and does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: What is scraping and what is scratching? Scraping is with small [teeth] and makes a wound. Scratching is with large [teeth] and does not make a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to define the two combing terms from the משנה. This sharpens the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition shows that קרצוף is fully permitted on its own, since it makes no wound. So the only possible reason to forbid it is a גזירה that he might come to do קידור. רבי יהודה does not make that גזירה, which strengthens the question on him.
steps.whyThisMatters: The definition removes any possibility that קרצוף is forbidden in itself. This isolates the question to whether רבי יהודה makes a protective גזירה, which the גמרא must now answer.

phrases.english: And it was taught: What is scraping
and what is scratching?
Scraping is with small [teeth],
and they make a wound.
Scratching is with large [teeth],
and they do not make a wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and sharpens the קשיא by defining the terms in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה permits an act whose only problem would be a גזירה (fear of escalating to a wound).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) defining קידור and קרצוף.

steps.title: A dying animal causes panic, but a suffering animal does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge from step 3. With a בכור, the animal may die, so the owner panics. With the comb, the animal only suffers, so there is no panic.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (the בכור), if he leaves it alone, it will die, so we say a person panics over his property. Here (the comb), if he leaves it alone, it is only pain, so we do not say a person panics over his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the question from step 3. It shows that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The level of panic depends on how much money is at stake. A dying בכור is a total loss, so the owner may act without thinking and make a מום. An animal stung by insects is only uncomfortable, so the owner stays calm, and there is no reason to forbid the gentle comb.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (our case: the comb on יום טוב)
A person panics over his property

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's worry about panic applies only when there is a serious loss, such as the animal dying. Simple discomfort is not enough.

phrases.english: There, if he leaves it alone, it will die,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the בכור with blood buildup.

phrases.english: so we say a person panics over his property.
Here, if he leaves it alone,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the animal on יום טוב that's bothered by insects.

phrases.english: it is merely pain,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן אָדָם בָּהוּל עַל מָמוֹנוֹ.
phrases.english: so we do not say a person panics over his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 3, now that step 4 has defined the two combs
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי יהודה contradicts himself about financial panic
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge compared a case where the animal could die to a case where it only suffers. These are different levels of loss.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by size of loss: a dying animal causes panic, mere discomfort does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה permits קרצוף without fearing escalation, it seemed he does not hold אדם בהול על ממונו at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה applies אדם בהול על ממונו only when the animal may die, as with the בכור. He does not apply it to mere pain, as with the comb.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה decree about חמץ but not about combing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה makes a protective decree about חמץ, since he does not make one about the gentle comb.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה: what is different about חמץ, that he made a decree, and what is different about the gentle comb, that he did not make a decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new contradiction in רבי יהודה's approach. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חמץ, רבי יהודה is worried that a person will mix up the permitted with the forbidden, so he makes a גזירה. With the combs he has no such worry and allows the gentle comb. The גמרא wants to know why he is strict in one place and relaxed in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (a request to explain a distinction)
Scratching with a large-toothed comb that does not wound

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda,
what is different about leaven, that he decreed,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי קִרְצוּף דְּלָא גָּזַר?
phrases.english: and what is different about scratching, that he did not decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי חָמֵץ דְּגָזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge after the panic question was settled
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה's protective decrees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה worries about a mix-up with חמץ but not with the combs. Why should these cases differ?

steps.title: Bread is easily confused with bread, but two combs are not
steps.stepSummary: Two kinds of bread look alike and get mixed up. The two combs are different tools, so no one confuses them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bread with bread: it gets confused. Wounding-comb with scratching-comb: it does not get confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. A decree is needed only where a real mix-up is likely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitted bread and forbidden bread look almost the same, so a person can easily slip from one to the other. The two combs are completely different tools, with small teeth versus large teeth, so a person will not accidentally use the forbidden one.

keyTerms.meaning: Scraping with a small-toothed comb that makes a wound

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה against confusion is made only where the permitted and forbidden things really look alike.

phrases.english: Bread with bread can be interchanged.
Scraping with scratching cannot be interchanged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases based on how likely confusion is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seems inconsistent about making protective decrees
steps.terutzMaskana: He decrees only where confusion is realistic: bread with bread, but not one comb with another

steps.title: New משנה: how late on ערב פסח one may eat חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says one may eat through the fifth hour and burn at the start of the sixth. רבי יהודה says one may eat through the fourth hour, must hold off in the fifth, and burn at the start of the sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי מאיר says: We eat the whole fifth hour and burn at the beginning of the sixth. רבי יהודה says: We eat the whole fourth hour, hold off the whole fifth, and burn at the beginning of the sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a dispute about the deadline for eating חמץ on the 14th of ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that חמץ is burned at the start of the sixth hour. They disagree about the fifth hour. רבי מאיר allows eating then, while רבי יהודה says the fifth hour is a 'hold' hour (תולין), when one neither eats nor burns.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold it off: we neither eat nor burn yet
The beginning of the sixth hour

steps.confusionAlert: 'Hours' here are counted from the start of the day, not by clock time. The sixth hour ends at midday.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Meir says:
One eats the entire fifth hour,
and burns at the beginning of the sixth.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
One eats the entire fourth hour,
holds it in abeyance the entire fifth,
and burns at the beginning of the sixth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אוֹכְלִים כׇּל חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion has ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ is burned at the start of the sixth hour. רבי מאיר allows eating in the fifth hour, while רבי יהודה allows eating only through the fourth and treats the fifth as a hold period.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical deadlines for eating and destroying חמץ on ערב פסח.

steps.title: The two תודה loaves as a public time signal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה describes two disqualified תודה loaves placed on a bench in the בית המקדש. Removing one loaf signaled the people to stop eating. Removing both signaled them to burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה said further: Two disqualified loaves of a תודה were laid on the bench. As long as they lay there, all the people ate. When one was removed, they held off: they neither ate nor burned. When both were removed, all the people began burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds how the public knew what time it was. The loaves acted as a signal for the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This signal matches רבי יהודה's three stages. Both loaves showing means eat. One loaf showing means hold off, in the fifth hour. No loaves means burn, at the start of the sixth hour.

keyTerms.meaning: A bench in the colonnade of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה there are three stages: eat (through the fourth hour), hold off (the fifth hour), and burn (the start of the sixth). The two loaves signaled each stage to the public.

phrases.english: And furthermore Rabbi Yehuda said:
Two disqualified loaves of a thanks-offering
are placed on the bench,
as long as they are placed there,
the entire nation eats.
When one was taken away, they hold off;
they neither eat nor burn.
When both were taken away,
the entire nation began burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת שֶׁל תּוֹדָה פְּסוּלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by giving the public signal for רבי יהודה's three stages
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The removal of the two תודה loaves told the people when to stop eating and when to burn their חמץ.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's middle position
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל splits the timing. חולין may be eaten through the fourth hour, תרומה through the fifth, and all חמץ is burned at the start of the sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: regular food may be eaten all of the fourth hour, תרומה all of the fifth hour, and we burn at the start of the sixth hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion, from רבן גמליאל, about how long one may eat חמץ on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל agrees with רבי יהודה that ordinary food must stop after the fourth hour. But he gives תרומה an extra hour, because eating תרומה is a מצוה and burning it is a loss. Everyone, including him, burns at the start of the sixth hour.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן
At the start of the sixth hour

steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions. רבי מאיר: eat through the fifth hour. רבי יהודה: eat through the fourth, hold off in the fifth. רבן גמליאל: חולין through the fourth, תרומה through the fifth. All three agree that burning happens at the start of the sixth hour.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Non-sacred food may be eaten the entire fourth hour,
and teruma the entire fifth hour,
phrases.notes: Extra time is given because eating תרומה is a מצוה, and burning it wastes holy food.

phrases.english: and we burn at the beginning of the sixth hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה dispute from step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין may be eaten through the fourth hour and תרומה through the fifth; burning is at the start of the sixth.

steps.title: Witnesses off by one day: testimony stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere. If one witness says the second of the month and the other says the third, the testimony is valid. One witness may not have known the previous month was made longer by a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: one witness says it happened on the second of the month, and another says on the third. Their testimony stands, because this one knew that a day was added to the month, and that one did not know a day was added.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a משנה from another place, about witnesses who do not match exactly. This is a setup: the גמרא is preparing to compare it to our משנה's dispute about time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, witnesses who contradict each other are thrown out. Here a one-day difference is explained innocently. One witness knew בית דין made the last month 30 days long (עיבור), and the other did not. So they are really describing the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding a day to the month, making it 30 days long
The discussion that analyzes the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses are not lying or careless. Both mean the same actual day. They just count the days of the month differently.

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in סנהדרין about witnesses who contradict each other.

phrases.english: One witness says on the second of the month,
and one says on the third —
their testimony stands,
because this one knows about the extension of the month,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּעִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and that one does not know about the extension of the month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by bringing an outside משנה as a basis for comparison
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-day mismatch in the date does not cancel testimony, since it can be explained by not knowing about עיבור החודש.

steps.title: How big a gap cancels testimony, per רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A two-day gap in the date cancels the testimony. For hours, a one-hour gap (second vs. third) is allowed, but a two-hour gap (third vs. fifth) cancels it. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: One says the third of the month and one says the fifth: their testimony is void. One says at two hours and one says at three hours: their testimony stands. One says at three and one says at five: their testimony is void. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה continues by setting the limits: which gaps between witnesses are forgivable and which cancel the testimony. It names רבי מאיר as the source, which sets up the comparison to his view in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A two-day gap cannot be explained by עיבור, since only one day is ever added. With hours, רבי מאיר accepts a one-hour gap (two vs. three) but not a two-hour gap (three vs. five). אביי will explain exactly how much error, if any, this implies (Steps 14–19).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי מאיר's limit for time errors here (one hour forgiven, two not) will be compared to his ruling in our משנה. That is how the גמרא checks whether רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are consistent across both topics.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בַּחֲמִשָּׁה —
phrases.english: One says on the third, and one says on the fifth —
their testimony is void.
phrases.notes: Only one day can be added to a month, so a two-day gap cannot be explained.

phrases.english: One says at two hours,
and one says at three hours —
their testimony stands.
One says at three,
and one says at five —
their testimony is void,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בַּחֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה, setting the limits of acceptable mismatch
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a two-day date gap or a two-hour time gap cancels testimony; a one-hour gap does not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה accepts a two-hour gap, but five versus seven is impossible
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says witnesses who say 'third hour' and 'fifth hour' still have valid testimony. But if one says five and the other says seven, the testimony is void. At five the sun is in the east, and at seven it is in the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: their testimony stands. If one says at five and one says at seven, their testimony is void. At five the sun is in the east, and at seven the sun is in the west.
steps.whatsHappening: The outside משנה finishes. רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר about the third-versus-fifth case, and then the משנה gives a case that everyone agrees is void.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, רבי מאיר voided testimony where one witness said three and the other said five. רבי יהודה says a mistake that big is still possible, so the testimony stands. Five versus seven is different, because the sun has visibly crossed from east to west, so no one could confuse those two hours.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'hours' here are counted from sunrise, so the fifth hour is before midday and the seventh hour is after midday. That is why the sun's direction gives the time away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יהודה allows a wider margin of error in telling time than רבי מאיר. That fits his stricter timeline for חמץ (Step 8), where he makes people hold off during the fifth hour as a safety buffer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: their testimony stands.
phrases.notes: This refers to the third-hour vs. fifth-hour case from Step 12.

phrases.english: If one says at five,
and one says at seven —
their testimony is void.
For at five the sun is in the east,
and at seven the sun is in the west.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the outside משנה by giving רבי יהודה's disagreement with רבי מאיר's ruling in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a two-hour gap (three vs. five) is acceptable. A gap that crosses midday (five vs. seven) voids the testimony according to everyone.

steps.title: אביי measures how much a person can err in each view
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the size of the mistake each תנא allows. According to רבי מאיר, a person does not err at all. According to רבי יהודה, a person can err by half an hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When you analyze it, according to רבי מאיר a person does not err at all; according to רבי יהודה a person errs by half an hour.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a headline rule for how much timing error each תנא accepts. He sets this up here and explains it in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is surprising that רבי מאיר would allow 'no error,' since he accepts a one-hour gap. אביי will show that the two witnesses can both be exactly right. It is also surprising that רבי יהודה allows only half an hour, since he accepts a two-hour gap. אביי will show that two half-hour errors in opposite directions are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: When you analyze it, you will find you can say

phrases.english: Abaye said: When you analyze it, you will find you can say:
According to the words of Rabbi Meir —
a person does not err at all;
according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda —
a person errs by half an hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה just completed to find the exact margin of error behind each view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: zero error. רבי יהודה: up to half an hour of error.

steps.title: How רבי מאיר's view works with zero error
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the event happened exactly as the second hour ended and the third began. The witness who said 'second' meant its very end, and the witness who said 'third' meant its very beginning. Both are correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר a person does not err at all: when the incident happened, it was as the second hour was going out and the third was coming in. The one who said 'two' meant the end of two, and the one who said 'three' meant the beginning of three.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the first half of his rule. He shows how רבי מאיר can accept a one-hour gap without saying anyone made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses seem to contradict each other, but they are describing the same moment from two sides of the hour line. So in Step 12 רבי מאיר is not allowing for a mistake. He accepts the testimony because both witnesses can be completely accurate. A two-hour gap cannot be explained this way, which is why he voids it.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — אֵין אָדָם טוֹעֶה וְלֹא כְּלוּם:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir — a person does not err at all:
when the incident happened,
it was as two was ending and three was beginning.
phrases.notes: This is the exact border between the second and third hours.

phrases.english: And the one who said 'two' meant the end of two,
and the one who said 'three' meant the beginning of three.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — אֵין אָדָם טוֹעֶה וְלֹא כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבי מאיר half of אביי's rule from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, testimony that differs by one hour is valid only because both witnesses can be exactly right at the border between the hours.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה's view works with half-hour errors
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, the event happened in the middle of the fourth hour. One witness said 'end of three' and was half an hour too early. The other said 'beginning of five' and was half an hour too late.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה a person errs by half an hour: when the incident happened, it was in the middle of the fourth hour. The one who said three meant the end of three, and he cut off half an hour forward. The one who said five meant the beginning of five, and he cut off half an hour backward.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the second half of his rule. He shows how רבי יהודה can accept a three-versus-five gap while assuming each witness is off by only half an hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Place the event at 3:30 (the middle of the fourth hour). The 'three' witness meant the end of the third hour (3:00), so he is 30 minutes early. The 'five' witness meant the start of the fifth hour (4:00), so he is 30 minutes late. Each witness made only a small half-hour mistake, and so the testimony holds together.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts off, i.e., is off by (errs by)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Beginning of five' here means the start of the fifth hour (4:00 after sunrise), not 5:00. So the two witnesses are really only one hour apart in their meaning, each 30 minutes off from 3:30.
steps.whyThisMatters: This view explains רבי יהודה's extra waiting hour for חמץ (Step 8). Since people can be off in their sense of time, he builds in a margin of safety.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — אָדָם טוֹעֶה חֲצִי שָׁעָה:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda — a person errs by half an hour:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה כִּי הֲוָה, בְּפַלְגָא דְאַרְבַּע הֲוָה,
phrases.english: when the incident happened, it was in the middle of the fourth hour,
and this one who said 'three' meant the end of three,
and he is off by half an hour too early.
And this one who said 'five' meant the beginning of five,
and he is off by half an hour too late.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — אָדָם טוֹעֶה חֲצִי שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבי יהודה half of אביי's rule from Step 14 and completes the first version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, each witness may be off by up to half an hour in opposite directions, so 'three' and 'five' can describe the same moment.
steps.whatToRemember: First version of אביי: רבי מאיר allows no error, because both witnesses are exactly right at an hour border. רבי יהודה allows half an hour of error for each witness, in opposite directions.

steps.title: A second version of אביי: a bit of error versus an hour and a bit
steps.stepSummary: Some report אביי differently. According to רבי מאיר, a person errs by a tiny bit. According to רבי יהודה, a person errs by an hour and a bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אביי said: When you analyze it, according to רבי מאיר a person errs a bit; according to רבי יהודה a person errs an hour and a bit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what אביי said. This line gives the headline, and the next steps explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, only one witness is wrong, and he carries the whole gap himself. That is why the margins are larger than in the first version: a small bit for רבי מאיר, and more than a full hour for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Some say: Abaye said:
When you analyze it, you will find you can say:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — אָדָם טוֹעֶה מַשֶּׁהוּ;
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Meir — a person errs a bit;

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — אָדָם טוֹעֶה שָׁעָה וּמַשֶּׁהוּ.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda — a person errs an hour and a bit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing report of אביי's statement from Step 14, with different error sizes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second version: רבי מאיר allows a tiny error, and רבי יהודה allows an hour and a bit.

steps.title: רבי מאיר in the second version: one witness is slightly off
steps.stepSummary: The event happened either at the end of the second hour or at the start of the third. One of the two witnesses is off by a tiny bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר a person errs a bit: when the incident happened, it was either at the end of two or at the beginning of three, and one of them errs by a bit.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version explains רבי מאיר. The event was on one side of the hour line or the other, so one witness was just slightly wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 15), the event was exactly on the line, so no one erred. Here we say the event fell just before or just after the line. So one witness crossed into the wrong hour by a tiny moment, and רבי מאיר allows that small mistake.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — אָדָם טוֹעֶה מַשֶּׁהוּ:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir — a person errs a bit:
when the incident happened,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּסוֹף שְׁתַּיִם הֲוָה אוֹ בִּתְחִלַּת שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: it was either at the end of two or at the beginning of three,
and one of them errs by a bit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — אָדָם טוֹעֶה מַשֶּׁהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבי מאיר half of the second version from Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one witness may be off by a tiny moment across the hour line.

steps.title: רבי יהודה in the second version: one witness is off by over an hour
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה in this version, the event happened either at the end of the third hour or at the beginning of the fifth. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה a person errs an hour and a bit: when the incident happened, it was either at the end of three or at the beginning of five,
steps.whatsHappening: The second version starts to explain רבי יהודה. The sentence breaks off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The event was at one edge of the gap: either the end of the third hour or the start of the fifth. Whichever witness named the other edge skipped the whole fourth hour plus a bit. That is the 'hour and a bit' error that רבי יהודה allows.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the third hour
The beginning of the fifth hour
Four (the fourth hour, which lies between them)

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — אָדָם טוֹעֶה שָׁעָה וּמַשֶּׁהוּ:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda — a person errs an hour and a bit:
when the incident happened —

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּסוֹף שָׁלֹשׁ אוֹ בִּתְחִלַּת חָמֵשׁ,
phrases.english: it was either at the end of three or at the beginning of five,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — אָדָם טוֹעֶה שָׁעָה וּמַשֶּׁהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבי יהודה half of the second version from Step 17. It continues into the next passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, one witness may be off by the entire fourth hour plus a bit.
